title: Resilience injector: staged regional evacuation + GPU scarcity + upstream blackhole simulation
creator: Ariel Cortez
description:
Objective: Build and validate a reusable failure-injector harness and runbook for staged regional evacuation, GPU-pool scarcity, and upstream dependency blackholes to exercise our SLOs, circuit breakers, and load-shedding policies. The harness must run safely in staging and be runnable in production with strict guardrails (timeboxed, percentage-of-traffic, kill-switch).

Background: We have recurring uncertainty about how well our routing + fallback rules, admission-control, and cache policies behave under a combination of (1) sudden region loss, (2) GPU exhaustion within a region or pool, and (3) silent downstream dependencies (DB/feature-store/service) that appear healthy but drop or blackhole traffic. Past incidents showed slow failovers and runaway retry storms that burned error budget. This ticket implements a targeted test harness plus dashboards and a documented runbook.

Scope:
- Failure modes to simulate: region-level network partition (control-plane reachable, data-plane severed), controlled termination of a percentage of GPUs in a pool, artificial throttling / CPU/GPU contention on a subset of inference servers, and dependency blackholes (TCP SYN accepted but no response / RST / SYN drop depending on scenario).
- Integrations: routing layer (smart-router), admission controller, per-model circuit breakers, autoscaler signals, and Console metrics + traces.
- Safety: automatic abort on elevated customer-error-rate (>0.1% of baseline) or rapid error-budget burn, operator confirmation step for any production run.

Deliverables:
1) failure-injector service (k8s job + operator CLI) with scenario presets: regional-evacuate-staged, gpu-scarcity-gradual, upstream-silence, combined-stress.
2) standardized experiment definition format (.yaml) to declare traffic split, duration, scope (percentage of region/pool), success criteria, and rollback rules.
3) dashboards + alert rules showing SLO burn, p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth, batch sizes, admission-drop-count, circuit-breaker trips, and retry amplification.
4) playbook in Confluence describing step-by-step staging -> non-prod rehearsal -> prod dress rehearsal -> postmortem template.
5) One end-to-end staged run and one controlled production dress rehearsal with stakeholders present.

Non-goals: Full chaos grid (we'll build targeted scenarios only). Network-level simulation across cloud providers is out of scope; we will use provider APIs + routing rules for region-level tests where possible.
acceptance_criteria: Injector service can run all scenario presets in staging with no manual code changes
Experiment YAML supports percent-of-traffic and per-model scoping
Dashboards show pre/post experiment baselines and annotate experiment windows
Runbook includes explicit abort conditions and operator checklist
Two experiments executed: one in staging (automated) and one production dress rehearsal (manual, timeboxed), both with documented postmortems
tasks: Design experiment YAML schema and validator (open RFC)
Implement k8s Job + controller to orchestrate instance drain, tainting, and iptables rules
Add GPU throttling shim (cgroup cpuset/cpu quota + fake OOM signals) and graceful drain hooks
Implement dependency blackhole patterns (iptables DROP, TCP blackhole proxy, and latency-inject proxy)
Wire injector to Console: emit annotations and experiment IDs to traces/metrics
Create dashboards and SLO burn visualizations for experiment windows
Security review & approve operator permissions and kill-switch design
Run staged experiment; collect data and write postmortem
